objective: Publish one repository-wide Definition of Ready and one executable Exit Gate for the #309 multi-scenario epic and its child issues, standardize the fields those gates check, add reusable Issue and PR checklists that reference them, and provide a deterministic script that reports a PR body as READY, BLOCKED or INCOMPLETE against the checklist so an omission is detectable without a new workflow engine.
decision_supported: Can a reviewer determine from a pull request body alone whether every required readiness field and every required exit-gate item is present, and can a deterministic command reproduce that verdict instead of relying on a reviewer's memory?
acceptance: one Definition of Ready lists the required fields, the check that detects each one, and the reason it is required, and it is referenced from the project-management index and the Task Packet guide

one Exit Gate lists the closing conditions for an implementation pull request, including that the Task Packet matches the final diff, that a failure path was exercised, and that the checklist grants no merge, release or physical-validation authority

a deterministic script reports READY, BLOCKED or INCOMPLETE, exits 0, 1 or 2, applies the Definition of Ready to an issue body with --kind issue and the Exit Gate to a pull request body by default, and never executes the commands or approval checks it reads
the script rejects a pull request body that omits a required readiness item, leaves a checkbox unticked, or marks an item done without the evidence reference the checklist requires

the script refuses a body that claims a merge, release or physical-validation authority the checklist deliberately does not grant, without echoing the offending sentence into its own output or archive
the script reports an empty or unreadable body as INCOMPLETE rather than as READY or BLOCKED, and reports a gate definition it cannot enforce as INCOMPLETE rather than as a pass

the Issue template and the pull request template reference the committed gates by path so a reviewer can open the definition from the form itself, and --check-template fails when either template drifts from the definition
every rule the script enforces has a unit test covering the accepted case and the rejected case, and the rejected case for a forbidden claim is read from the rule's own declared sample
no production module, interface schema, contract model, firmware source or workflow file is modified by this change
evidence: Task Packet schema validation output with exit code
a --check-template run showing exit code 0, and a run over a drifted template showing exit code 1 and the named missing heading
a BLOCKED run over a body that claims merge authority the checklist does not grant
a BLOCKED run over the committed missing-evidence fixture showing exit code 1 and the named missing item
a READY run over the committed complete fixture showing exit code 0
a READY run over the committed issue fixture showing exit code 0, and a BLOCKED run over the same fixture with one readiness field removed
an INCOMPLETE run over an unreadable or empty body showing exit code 2 rather than a pass
final git diff --check and git diff --name-only output proving every changed path is allowed
mutation probe: with the Definition-of-Ready section check disabled, the issue-mode test that removes one field fails; the probe is restored byte-identically and confirmed with diff -q and sha256sum
mutation probe: with the checkbox rule disabled, the unticked-checkbox test fails; the probe is restored byte-identically and confirmed with diff -q
ruff check, ruff format --check, the full pytest run, make contract, make scenario-check, make golden-check, make context-check and make docs output with exit codes
targeted pytest output listing the collected Issue #310 test names, pass counts and exit codes
stop_conditions: Meeting the acceptance requires editing a workflow file, a production module, an interface schema or a contract model.
The checklist is enforced by a mechanism that can merge, release or certify a physical validation instead of only reporting a verdict.
A missing item is reported as READY instead of BLOCKED or INCOMPLETE.
The script executes any command or approval check it reads rather than only reporting presence.
data_classification: internal; every fixture is a synthetic pull request body with placeholder owners, synthetic paths and synthetic evidence references, and reads no real candidate, customer, credential or operator data
model_policy: no model call; presence and checkbox checking are deterministic and are never delegated to a model
risks_and_fallbacks: A checklist that nobody can execute degrades into prose. Every required item names the command or artifact that satisfies it, and the detector reports the item by name so the fix is unambiguous.

A readiness gate can quietly become a merge gate. The checklist states that it grants no merge, release or physical-validation authority, the script refuses a body that claims that authority, and no workflow file is touched by this change.

A detector that parses free text breaks on the first reformatting. The required items are section headings taken from the committed templates, so a template edit and a detector edit move together and a test pins the pairing.
A gate that passes on an empty body is worse than no gate. An unreadable, empty or unrecognized body reports INCOMPLETE with a non-zero exit rather than READY.

Reusing the Task Packet validator was considered and rejected: it validates the machine-readable packet, while this issue is about the reviewer-facing pull request body, and widening that script's contract would change an existing gate.

This issue depends on terminology that #308 owns. The documents defer to the multi-scenario contract for ownership boundaries and do not restate them, so a later #308 decision does not have to un-edit these files.
